Significant deficiencies will be reported via the final inspection report. 2. The SCAR Check Sheet reflects a series of questions to be asked to determine the accomplishment status of an MRC previously reported as accomplished. Although the sheet may be used as a reference for conducting a real time monitored MRC evaluation, for the purposes of conducting a 3MI, all spot checks will be conducted on accomplished (historic) MRCs. 3. Due to the nature of MRC completion, supporting programs such as Tag-Outs and HAZMAT are encountered. Care should be taken to avoid expanding the spot check to a review of the processes of those programs thereby preventing the assessor from determining the accomplishment status of the MRC under review. 4. The following is expanded guidance for completion of the SCAR Check Sheet. Best practices or other policies not supported by source documentation will not be included in evaluating compliance: a. (1.a). Determine if the MP is qualified to perform the maintenance task. PQS 301 is required for all MRCs but attention should also be paid to other qualifications required such as Quality Maintenance (see volume V, Part I, Chapter 3, paragraph 3.4 of this manual) or graduation from a required school such as gage calibration technician. b. (1.b). Determine if the correct TPMTE were used during the performance of the MRC.

If the MP did not have the required TPMTE, it is unlikely that they would have been able to complete all the procedural steps of the MRC as required. If an item of TPMTE was required to perform a conditional step and that step was not required to be accomplished, it is not considered deficient. If the required test equipment required calibration, ensure that the calibration is within date and the equipment is of sufficient scale to accomplish the MRC. c. (1.c). Determine if the MP maintained the correct equipment. d. (1.d). Examine the MRC to determine that any locally applied changes are authorized by procedural notes, external correspondence, or allowed by reference (a). e. (1.e). Determine applicability of the MRC to the component that the MP signed for completion. NOTE: IF A PROCEDURAL STEP WAS NOT COMPLETED, THE MRC SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN REPORTED AS COMPLETE AND THEREFORE THE ATTRIBUTE GRADE SHOULD BE ZERO AND ALL SUBSEQUENT ATTRIBUTES SHOULD ALSO BE ZERO, EFFECTIVELY “FAILING” THE SPOT CHECK. f. (2.a). From a variety of potential techniques, determine if the MP performed all the required steps of the MRC. This may be accomplished via re-enactment, a discussion regarding the steps or re-performance. The inspector should come away with a clear impression that all the steps of the MRC were either fully accomplished or not. NOTE: IF A REQUIRED TAG-OUT WAS NOT CONDUCTED IN SUPPORT OF ACCOMPLISHING THE MRC, THE MRC SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN CONDUCTED AND REPRESENTS A SERIOUS SAFETY VIOLATION. THEREFORE, THE ATTRIBUTE GRADE SHOULD BE ZERO AND ALL SUBSEQUENT ATTRIBUTES SHOULD ALSO BE ZERO EFFECTIVELY “FAILING” THE SPOT CHECK. g. (2.b). If required by the MRC, verify that a tag-out was hung before the maintenance was performed. Ensure the isolation boundaries were appropriately identified and correctly positioned to ensure complete isolation of the maintained equipment. If no tag-out was required, write NA on the sheet. NOTE:

FAILURE TO ADHERE TO A SAFETY PRECAUTION PROVIDED ON THE MRC CONSTITUTES A SERIOUS SAFETY VIOLATION AND THE FAILURE TO PERFORM THE MRC AS WRITTEN. THE ATTRIBUTE GRADE WILL BE ZERO AND ALL SUBSEQUENT ATTRIBUTES WILL ALSO BE ZERO, EFFECTIVELY “FAILING” THE SPOT CHECK. h. (2.c). Determine compliance with all specific safety precautions listed on the MRC. If no safety requirements were invoked, write NA on the sheet. i. (3.a). By physical examination of the maintained equipment, determine if maintenance of the nature required by the MRC had been performed. Take note of fasteners that would have had to be disturbed, dirt in filters, fresh oil, etc. to make a judgment as to whether the maintenance has been performed. NOTE: DUE TO THE POTENTIAL LIABILITY INCURRED BY IMPROPER USE AND DISPOSAL OF HAZMAT, SOME WCS HAVE ASSIGNED SPECIALLY TRAINED PERSONNEL TO PROVIDE HAZMAT AND DISPOSAL SERVICES FOR SURPLUS MATERIAL INSTEAD OF THE MP. THIS IS ACCEPTABLE PROVIDED THE INSPECTOR CAN DETERMINE FULL COMPLIANCE. j. (3.b). Determine through questioning and record verification that HAZMAT was properly used and disposed of as a means of determining whether the MRC was accomplished. Once the inspector has determined that the HAZMAT was used and disposed of correctly, this attribute is considered fulfilled. If no HAZMAT was required to be utilized, write NA on the sheet. k. (3.c). Determine if the MP could have performed the MRC from a standpoint of being trained and proficient in the tasks called out for by the procedure. l. (4.a). Determine if the MP filled out the 13-Week Accountability Log or annotated proper disposition of maintenance in SKED correctly for the accomplished MRC with the appropriate accomplishment date. Ensure that if a tag-out isolation was used, the tag serial number is recorded in the space allowed or as a check note in SKED.

Ensure that the printed name and legal signature of the MP who performed the maintenance is recorded or, in case of group performed PMS, the MP in charge of the group. m. (4.b). From reviewing the discussions and findings during the spot check, determine if an FBR or PSR had been submitted if required. If no FBR or PSR was required, write NA on the sheet. n. (4.c). Determine if a material deficiency was noted during the PMS; if so, examine the CSMP to ensure the deficiency was documented. If no material deficiency was noted, write NA on the sheet. If material discrepancies are properly documented in the CSMP attribute graded as a two. Material discrepancies which are not documented in the CSMP will receive an automatic grade of zero. 5. When a Spot Check and monitor is determined to be below standards, the command undergoing inspection is likely to have numerous questions. To facilitate root cause analysis and the formulation of an effective corrective action plan, care should be taken to clearly identify factors contributing to deficiencies that led to the conclusion that the MRC was not conducted as written or not conducted at all. VOLUME VI CHAPTER 19-6 NAVAL SURFACE FORCES REFERENCES. (a) OPNAVINST 4790.4 - Ship's Maintenance and Material Management System Policy (b) NAVSEAINST 4790.8 - Ships’ Maintenance and Material Management (3-M) Manual (c) COMNAVSURFPAC/COMNAVSURFLANTINST 3502.3 - Surface Force Readiness Manual (d) NAVEDTRA 43241 - Personnel Qualification Standard for Ship’s Maintenance and Material Management (3-M) System (e) NAVEDTRA 43119 - Personnel Qualification Standard for Damage Control (DC) Watches (f) NAVEDTRA 43523 - Personnel Qualification Standard for Quality Maintenance Program (g) NAVSEA S0400-AD-URM-010/TUM - Tag-Out Users Manual (h) COMNAVSURFPAC/COMNAVSURFLANTINST 3502.7 - Surface Force Readiness and Training Manual (SFTRM) APPLICABILITY. All content of the Commander Naval Surface Force Pacific Fleet (COMNAVSURFPAC) and Commander Naval Surface Force Atlantic Fleet (COMNAVSURFLANT) 3-M Instruction has been incorporated into this chapter to provide easier access to 3-M guidance and requirements. PURPOSE. To issue Maintenance and Material Management (3-M) program requirements within COMNAVSURFPAC and COMNAVSURFLANT. The 3-M program is executed per references (a) through (h) and as clarified by this instruction. The goal is to maintain an effective unit maintenance program that will ensure a high state of material readiness. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES. a. Type Commander. The Type Commander (TYCOM) exercises primary responsibility for the effective operation and support of the 3-M System. Areas of responsibility include but are not limited to the following: (1) Ensure each unit has authorized programs: (a) Maintenance Data System (MDS) system installed. (b) Planned Maintenance System (PMS) Scheduling (SKED software).

(2) Ensure ships and units are manned with Navy Enlisted Classification (NEC) qualified Maintenance and Material Management Coordinators (3MC). (3) Be the certifying authority of all 3-M certifications. (4) Oversee surface Force 3-M representatives, including periodically observing 3-M representatives conducting 3-M Virtual Assessments (VA) and training events. (5) Review and approve curriculum content for Maintenance University and Surface Force Representative 3-M Training. b. Immediate Superior In Command. The Immediate Superior in Command (ISIC) is responsible but are not limited to reviewing the status of assigned unit’s 3-M pillars from detailed reports provided from Surface Force 3-M Representatives assigned to units. c. Afloat Training Group. Afloat Training Group will fill the role as the Surface Force 3-M Representatives and areas of responsibility include but are not limited to the following: (1) Monitor the assigned unit’s Maintenance Accomplishment Rate (MAR) utilizing the 3-M 365 Virtual Snap-Shot Report weekly. (2) Monitor the assigned unit’s Spot Check Program utilizing the 3-M 365 Virtual Snap-Shot Report weekly. (3) Monitor the assigned unit’s Current Ships Maintenance Project (CSMP) management utilizing the 3-M 365 CSMP Self-Sufficiency Report monthly at a minimum. (4) Monitor the assigned unit’s Knowledge, Skills, and Experience (KSE) utilizing the 3-M 365 KSE Analysis Report quarterly at a minimum. (5) Train assigned units on conducting CSMP Reconciliation and aligning the CSMP in the MDS. (6) Conduct command level training for all assigned Work Center Supervisors, Leading Chief Petty Officers, Division Officers and Department Heads as required to maintain the KSE. (7) Conduct Command Level Effectiveness Reviews (CLERs) for all subordinate commands quarterly per 3-M 365 Surface Force Representative standard operating procedure. (8) Schedule and participate in Program Validations for unit’s failing to meet 3-M 365 Pillar of Performance standards.

(9) Assist assigned units with preparing to enter or exit a Chief of Naval Operations Availability as defined in Volume II, Part I, Chapter 3 of this manual. (10) Submit a bi-weekly report to TYCOM containing all assigned unit performance metrics. (11) Submit training muster sheets to TYCOM as required. d. Commanding Officer or Officer in Charge. The Commanding Officer (CO) or Officer In Charge (OIC) is responsible for maintaining an effective 3-M program. The CO or OIC will: (1) Designate a 3MC in writing. (2) Conduct rigorous 3-M self-assessments. (3) Chair the Planning Board for Maintenance (PB4M). (4) Ensure material deficiencies are properly documented in the CSMP and tracked to resolution. (5) Conduct Spot Check the Spot Checker assessments to perform a Quality Assurance evaluation of the command’s Spot Check Program. (6) Assault Craft Unit, Beach Master Unit, Naval Beach Unit and Amphibious Construction Battalion may designate the detachment OIC to perform Department Head (DH) 3-M functions. All designations must be in writing and signed by the CO. (7) Ticonderoga and Arleigh Burke Class COs may designate in writing the Weapons Officer to perform DH 3-M functions for the following Work Centers (WC): CA01, CA02, CG01, CG02, CG03, CG04, CM01, CM02, and CM03 only. (8) Surface Force ships may have a billeted Plans and Tactics Officer. Plans and Tactics (PT) department will be an MDS only department. The PT department will NOT have responsibility for maintenance, PMS, or configuration management. e. Executive Officer. The Executive Officer (XO) is the command’s 3-M System Manager responsible to the CO for the overall management of the 3-M Program. The XO will: (1) Chair quarterly 3-M System meetings with DH and the 3MC. (2) Brief the CO on the status of 3-M.

The brief will include results from the Virtual Snap-Shot, CSMP Reconciliation, CSMP Self-Sufficiency, and KSE Reports. (3) Serve as the CO’s principal assistant for management of all on-ship (TA 4) maintenance. (4) Maintain an aggressive 3-M spot check program involving all levels of the Chain of Command (CoC) from the First Class Petty Officer (FCPO) to the CO. (5) Conduct Spot Check the Spot Checker assessments to perform a Quality Assurance evaluation of the command’s Spot Check Program. (6) Authorize shifts of maintenance responsibility between departments. (7) Maintain a command Zone Inspection program. f. Command Master Chief. The Command Master Chief will: (1) Attend the XO’s quarterly 3-M System meetings providing senior enlisted feedback. (2) Conduct Spot Check the Spot Checker assessments to perform a Quality Assurance evaluation of the command’s Spot Check Program. g. Command 3-M Coordinator. The 3MC will: (1) Serve as the key 3-M System assistant to the XO. (2) Maintain current directives, policies, and instructions. (3) Send Virtual Snap Shot, CSMP Reconciliation, CSMP Self Sufficiency results to the Surface Force 3-M Representative. A Plan of Actions and Milestones will be submitted for all scores from Virtual Snap-Shot and CSMP Self Sufficiency in “Red” (below standards) and discrepancies identified from the CSMP Reconciliation report. (4) Monitor the Ship’s 3-M Personnel Qualification Standards (PQS) Program and maintain an auditable record of personnel qualified in 3-M PQS. In ships R-Admin, ASM or any other installed program that tracks PQS and training, develop following training items for capture of TYCOM training as below: (a) 3-M TYCOM Office direct. (b) 3-M Advance SKED ANTECH. (c) 3-M Advance MDS from COMNAVSURFPAC N41. (d) 3-M TYCOM Representative training for Work Center Supervisor (WCS), Lead Chief Petty Officers (LCPO), DIVO and DH.

(e) Maintain command Change Service Accountability Log (CSAL). (f) Develop and maintain the master split Maintenance Index Page (MIP) tracker and ensure applicable split MIPs are appropriately assigned to affected WCs. (g) Ensure the Technical Librarian is maintaining the Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) Advanced Technical Information Support (ATIS) and WebATIS program are operational. (h) Develop and administer the ship or unit’s PMS Spot Check Program. (i) Ensure a complete back up of the SKED system is made on removable media (e.g. Digital Video Disk (DVD) or Compact Disk (CD)) following completion of the FR update and retain as part of the PMS Master File. If the 3MC is able to access locally stored report if network is down, then not required to save to external source. (j) Ensure command’s 26-week maintenance outlook report is electronically saved on removable media (e.g. DVD or CD) after all WCs have closed out weekly from SKED. If the 3MC is able to access locally stored report if network is down, then not required to save to external source. (k) Notify Surface Force 3-M Representative anytime Naval Tactical Command Support System (NTCSS), Maintenance Figure of Merit, Automated Work Notification (AWN), ATIS or SKED are unavailable. (l) Maintain an effective MDS program. (m) Maintain an effective PMS program. (n) Request authorization to delay implementation of the Force Revision to TYCOM Force 3MC via the Surface Force 3-M Representative. (o) Maintain access to the following programs: 1 RADWEB 2 PMS-MIS 3 WEBATIS 4 MCMS 5 ATM (Ashore AWN for AWN Platforms only) 6 COMNAVSURFPAC 3-M SharePoint h. Ship’s Maintenance and Material Officer. The Ship’s Maintenance and Material Officer (SMMO) has cognizance of the material condition of the ship. In that capacity, the SMMO will: (1) Coordinate the execution of PB4M.

(2) Serve as the CO’s principal assistant for management of all off-ship (TA 1, TA 2 and TA 3) brokered maintenance. (3) Conduct monthly command CSMP to shore Validation Screening and Brokering (VSB) file reconciliation. (4) Develop and provide Ship’s Force work package to the executing activity and assist in coordinating Ship’s Force work with the executing activity during availabilities. (5) Review all work candidates for WC ES01 monthly. Ensure TA 1, 2 and 3 jobs are planned for upcoming availabilities. Ensure all TA 4 jobs are sent to correct work centers and are rewritten under the work center with reference to ES01 job. Once a new job is written to correct material deficiency, close the original ES01 job. (6) Conduct the DH review for WC ES01. (7) Ensure the ship’s initial conditions are established for work prior to start by outside activities. Training Officer (1) Implement a short-range and long-range training plan per reference (a). (2) Notify WCS when: (a) MRC is not fully understood, appears to be incorrect or cannot be accomplished as written. (b) There are issues with the TPMTE block of the MRC. (c) The technician has doubts concerning his or her ability to perform the maintenance. (d) Equipment deficiencies or casualties are discovered. SHIPBOARD MAINTENANCE Preventative Maintenance System. PMS constitutes the scheduling and accomplishment of all periodic and situational maintenance conducted on shipboard equipment. All PMS is scheduled and completion reported via the SKED program. a. Qualifications and Accountability. The key to a successful 3-M Program is having highly-trained, knowledgeable, and qualified maintenance personnel accomplishing the maintenance. All personnel must complete the corresponding Personnel Qualification Standards (PQS) for their assigned billet associated to the 3-M program per references (c), (d) and (e). b. SKED guidance and utilization. (1) Guidance for use of SKED is provided via the SKED users guide with help menus, and wizards associated with SKED functionality.

(2) The Navy PMS DVD or CD-ROM is used to update the command or unit’s SKED PMS data. Electronic backup of the command or unit’s SKED database will be used to restore SKED databases. (3) The SKED program uses days to schedule and keep track of calendar periodicities. MRCs are displayed as out of periodicity when they fall outside the established date ranges in the SKED program. These date ranges are as reflected in Table 19-6-1 of this chapter. SKED Program Failure And Restoration. SKED Program failure. In the event of a SKED failure, operation of PMS performance and tracking is as follows: a. The 3MC will notify CoC and TYCOM immediately upon loss of system, or if planned outage will last longer than seven days and report status of backups. b The 3MC will utilize electronically saved copy of 26-week outlook report, situational requirements page, MIPs, MRCs available on Tailored Force Revision (TFR) DVD and distribute to WCs. c. Work Center Supervisors will utilize paper 13-week accountability logs (available on FR DVD) and will manually fill out maintenance required within their WCs and sign for completed maintenance. d. Work Center Supervisors will verify situational requirements page to ensure they do not miss scheduling situational checks. e. Work Center Supervisors will ensure MPs annotate tag-out number in the required block. Work Center Supervisors will identify checks that have mandatory related maintenance, and ensure there is an alphanumeric code assigned to parent check and all associated related checks. f. LCPOs will review and sign the 13-Week Accountability Log at the end of the PMS week and ensure checks added that week are hand-written into the blank accountability log. g. DIVOs will review sheets weekly to ensure 13-week accountability logs are complete. h Once SKED is confirmed back in operation, the 3MC will notify all hands. In the event of a SKED restoration, operation of PMS performance and tracking is as follows: (1) Each WCS will have to manually arrange SKED to match 13-week accountability logs.

Maintenance personnel will use SKED PIN as applicable to annotate completion of maintenance. Check notes and alert notes will be made per standard SKED entries as directed by sub-paragraph 19-6.4.9.f of this chapter (2) Once SKED has been updated to the current week, normal accounting for maintenance will resume. (3) If the 3MC turned off SKED PIN feature to ease the burden of catching the system back up, then paper 13-week accountability logs will have to be maintained for 13 weeks. They can be scanned and kept on the WC’s electronic folder on the LAN, Intranet. (4) If the 3MC did not turn SKED PIN feature off, once SKED matches the 13- week accountability logs exactly, then the paper reports can be disposed of. The WCS or LCPO will maintain the assignment of PMS with the Maintenance Outlook Report until SKED is restored. (5) Re-enable SKED PIN feature if previously turned off. Minimum Standards. MRC accomplishment is critical for maintaining equipment in a ready state and achieving expected service life. The maintenance tasks directed by MRCs are the minimum standards for organizational (shipboard) preventative maintenance and therefore equipment degradation can be assumed if maintenance is deferred. The following provisions are provided to maximize on time performance of PMS and provide increased fleet latitude in maintaining equipment. a. MRCs are prepared as instructions to complete a maintenance task based upon the premise that the personnel assigned to perform the task have sufficient knowledge of the rate listed on the card and are qualified to perform maintenance as directed by the MRC. The MRC will be accomplished in sequential order, adhering to all Warnings, Cautions and Notes. Routine sub-steps (e.g., fastener removal, steps to don and remove Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE), turning on a vacuum) may or may not be included in the MRC and their absence should not prevent the maintainer from completing the maintenance task. b. Per NAVSEA, procedures are written at a level of detail based on the assumption maintenance personnel are trained, qualified and supervised by experienced leadership to execute the maintenance consistently and expertly.

They exist to provide a common standard, specify acceptance criteria, communicate warnings and cautions specific to the maintenance and provide proven maintenance practices. They are not intended to: (1) Supplement or duplicate rules and procedures that must be followed for hazards generally associated with the equipment (Hazardous Material Handling, Electrical Shock Risk Management, etc.) but not specifically associated with a step of the procedure. (2) Identify every process and every warning associated with the maintenance environment of the component being maintained (aloft, in tanks, near an active flight deck, in a heat stress area, etc.). (3) Specify every possible action of the maintainer. c. Leadership will uphold standards for complying with maintenance procedures. This standard does not mean the maintainer is expected to robotically follow the MRC word-by-word. Leadership, trainers, monitors, auditors and inspectors should not expect it. The key word here is “intent”. The objective is to perform the intent of each step (not necessarily step-by-step) performance. d. If a step is missing that is necessary to complete the task and that step is not obvious to the Maintenance Person (MP), an FBR should be submitted. e. MRC completion status is dependent on the accomplishment of all procedural steps on all of the equipment listed on the MRC or its accompanying Location Guide List. f. The performance of additional rational actions during the accomplishment of a MRC is authorized. Examples of such actions include turning on and off items utilized during the performance of the MRC (vacuum cleaners, test equipment, etc.) and general housekeeping (cleaning up or containing spilled fluids or dirt). g. The substitution of any tools, materials or test equipment not held by the activity should be considered prior to deciding to defer the maintenance until the exact tools, materials or test equipment listed on the MRC are procured. This is especially critical for frequently required maintenance where several performance cycles can be missed while waiting for supply to provide the correct items. Substitution requirements are provided by reference (a) and other technical documents. Functional Components. a. PMS Master File.

The Master File, maintained by the ship or unit’s 3MC, contains information relative to PMS requirements that are specific to equipment for which the command is responsible. The Master File provides for duplicate issue of missing MIPs and MRCs, contains supplementary information provided by NAVSEA Logistics Center (NAVSEALOGCEN) Detachments Norfolk or San Diego and serves as a repository for changes received between FR distributions, which must be retained on file until the changes are reflected in a subsequent FR. b. PMS Administrative Requirements. In lieu of a WC or Master File the following should be retained: (1) Hard copy Change Service Accountability Log: The CSAL will now shift to only 3MC managing one CSAL electronically stored on Local Area Network (LAN), Intranet or SKED help tab etc. that all hands have access to view. This will hold all command changes (Force Revision (FR) dates, Advanced Change Notice (ACN), FBRs, Significant system down time, etc.) to the 3-M Program. The WC Journal Tab in SKED houses all the changes the WC has made to their individual program (revisions, lineouts, custom notes, weekly closeouts, alert acknowledgements, check notes, alert notes, etc.). (2) Service Brief: Will be electronically stored on LAN, Intranet or SKED help tab etc. that all hands have access to view. Upon FBR implementation, a custom note on the affected MRC will be created that will house the FBR number; changes directed or can paste the entire FBR response. The WC’s LOEP will be verified by using the SKED LOEP Manager, all listed MIPs should say “normal”, if “On WC not on LOEP” or “Not on WC on LOEP” is listed, and the FBR log should be reviewed for approved FBRs that added or removed the MIP from the WC.
