VOLUME VI CHAPTER 34 FLIGHT DECK NON-SKID INSPECTION REFERENCES. (a) OPNAVINST 4700.7 - Maintenance Policy for U.S. Naval Ships (b) COMNAVAIRFORINST 4790.2 - Naval Aviation Maintenance Program (NAMP) (c) COMNAVSURFOR/COMNAVAIRFOR/COMMARFORCOM/COMMARFORPAC 4790.3 Instruction - Prevention of Foreign Object Damage (FOD) on CVN and LHD/LHA Class Ships (d) NAVSEA S9086-VD-STM-010 - NSTM Chapter 631 - Preservation of Ships in Service General (e) NAVSEA S9086-VG-STM-010 - NSTM Chapter 634 - Deck Coverings General (f) COMNAVSURFOR/COMNAVAIRFOR 9634.2 Instruction – Deck Nonskid Application, Inspection, Training, Quality Assurance and Reporting Procedures PURPOSE. The purpose of this section is to prevent Foreign Object Damage (FOD) to aircraft engines as it relates to flight deck non-skid, and to provide guidance on flight deck nonskid repair aboard Amphibious Class Ships and Aircraft Carriers conducting fixed wing aircraft operations. It is necessary to repair damaged non-skid in areas exposed to aircraft launch and recovery operations in a timely fashion in order to minimize risk of FOD to aircraft engines. Maintenance policy for ships is outlined in reference (a) and information regarding the Naval Aviation Maintenance Program is located within reference (b). The inspection of flight deck non-skid is to be accomplished prior to the first flight operation of the day per reference (c). BACKGROUND. a. Ingestion of foreign objects by gas turbine engines accounts for the largest percentage of premature engine removals from naval aircraft. FOD to an aircraft gas turbine engine caused by ingestion of flight deck non-skid can degrade engine performance and drive unscheduled removal and replacement of a damaged engine. Catastrophic engine failure from FOD may lead to loss of aircraft.

Additionally, FOD presents personnel and material hazards, consumes valuable maintenance man-hours, imposes additional unscheduled workloads, creates additional logistics requirements, wastes dollars, and reduces operational readiness. b. All non-skid materials will produce chips from daily wear associated with aircraft and ground support operations. Flight deck cleaning and FOD walk downs prior to flight operations are used as a precaution against ingestion of non-skid and other foreign objects by aircraft. c. Routine operations may damage flight deck non-skid. Wear and tear associated with helicopter landing skids, and the impacts of dropped or dragged heavy or sharp items may each result in damaged non-skid that exposes the flight deck bare metal surface. Corrosion associated with this bare metal eventually undercuts the non-skid in adjacent areas, leading to failure of the non-skid coating and a subsequent FOD risk. d. The consequences of damaged non-skid and the associate FOD risk make it imperative that damaged non-skid is repaired in a timely manner. SCOPE. This chapter applies to all Amphibious Warfare ships and Aircraft Carriers that conduct fixed-wing aircraft operations. RESPONSIBILITIES. Ship’s Force. a. The non-skid inspection and repair procedures described are accomplished by Ship’s Force, in order to provide early detection and treatment of corrosion and non-skid failures. Maintenance Requirement Cards contained within the Planned Maintenance System provide specific guidance for performing inspection of critical coated non-skid decks for corrosion and non-skid coating failure(s). Refer to reference (d) for boundary requirements for preparation and painting and critical coated decks are described in reference (e). b. The following actions apply to ship’s force when non-skid discrepancies are found: (1) Non-skid failure less than 36 square inches - Repair with primer no later than 28 days after discovery. (2) Non-skid failure greater than 36 inches and less than 50 square feet - Repair with non-skid system no later than 28 days after discovery. (3) Ship’s force will contact the Type Commander when areas of non-skid failure are greater than 50 square feet, or total area of non-skid failure is greater than 500 square feet.

Quality Assurance Officer (where assigned). Refer to Non-skid Quality Assurance Officer (QAO) for disposition of failed non-skid requiring submission of Work Request to Industrial Activity to repair or replace failed non-skid. Nonskid QAO is defined in reference (f). All nonskid existing or corrected problems/discrepancies must be listed in the Work Center's CSMP for history purposes.

VOLUME VI CHAPTER 35 REGIONAL MAINTENANCE CENTER I-LEVEL MAINTENANCE CAPABILITIES LISTING OF APPENDICES. A Regional Maintenance Center I-Level Maintenance Capability Matrix PURPOSE. This chapter provides a listing of Regional Maintenance Centers (RMC) I- Level maintenance capabilities for Surface Force ships and defines related reporting requirements. The Strike Force Intermediate Maintenance Activity (SFIMA), volume III, chapter 6 of this manual describes policies, provides governance and reporting requirements, and assigns roles, responsibilities, and actions necessary for Strike Group units. BACKGROUND. The primary mission of an RMC is to promote surface ship readiness via assessment, troubleshooting, and repair of systems and equipment which are beyond the technical capability or capacity of Fleet units. A secondary mission of an RMC is to provide enough production work experience and on-the-job training to sailors for them to improve their technical knowledge and, where appropriate, earn a Navy Enlisted Classification (NEC) code used to fill Navy Afloat Maintenance Training Strategy (NAMTS) billets when returning to sea duty. An RMC accomplishes both of these missions, in part, with the sustainment and utilization of their I-Level maintenance capability. Onboard Support. In addition to ship-to-shop and standard shipboard repair and maintenance work, the RMC I-Level capability is utilized to provide onboard Maintenance Assist Team (MAT) I-Level support to ships in port. The MAT concept was designed to bring RMC repair and maintenance training capability to bear on shipboard systems to improve Ship’s Force repair, self-assessment, maintenance and equipment operations capability. Applicable Regional Maintenance Centers. There are five RMCs with existing surface ship I-Level workforce: three of which are stand-alone Activities and two that are incorporated within Naval Shipyards. Southwest Regional Maintenance Center (SWRMC) is located in San Diego, CA. Hawaii Regional Maintenance Center (HRMC) is a function incorporated within Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PHNSY&IMF). Northwest Regional Maintenance Center (NWRMC) is a function incorporated within Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and IMF (PSNS&IMF).

NWRMC also includes Everett, WA maintenance operations. Mid Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center (MARMC) is located in Norfolk, VA. Southeast Regional Maintenance Center (SERMC) is located in Mayport, FL. RESPONSIBILITIES. Fleet Commanders. (individually or jointly, as appropriate). a. Approve changes, additions and deletions to the I-Level Capabilities Matrix (Appendix A) as recommended by the Type Commanders (TYCOM). b. Approve recommended changes to the NAMTS NEC At-Sea Requirements Matrix as provided by the TYCOMs. c. Approve and forward, with endorsement, NAMTS NEC modifications as developed and recommended by Commander, Navy Regional Maintenance Center (CNRMC) with TYCOM concurrence, to the Navy Enlisted Occupational Classification System Board. d. Review, approve and submit Billet Change Requests (BCR) developed by CNRMC, to support the sea and shore rotation requirements. e. Request additions and deletions to the I-Level capabilities listed in Appendix A and corresponding capacities at each RMC based on utilization metrics and written Business Case Analysis to the cognizant Fleet Commander. f. Ensure full utilization of the full range of organic RMC I-Level capability identified in Appendix A. g. Establish and communicate work priorities to CNRMC and cognizant RMCs. Resolve work priority conflicts as necessary. h. Regularly assess NAMTS maintenance skills required on respective afloat units. i. Approve CNRMC recommended, or recommend additional changes to specific NAMTS maintenance skills and required training for billets on respective afloat units. j. In collaboration with CNRMC, review and recommend NAMTS NEC At-Sea Requirements Matrix revisions to the cognizant Fleet Commander(s). k. Review and approve establishment and disestablishment of MATs, as recommended by CNRMC. Optimize utilization of MATs capacity within existing total I-Level workload in each cognizant RMC. Commander, Navy Regional Maintenance Center. CNRMC will: a. Provide the capabilities identified in Appendix A following all applicable policy, regulations and technical requirements.

Ensure detailed capability manuals are issued by each RMC to expound on and clarify the exact capabilities identified in Appendix A. b. Coordinate with the TYCOMs to ensure full utilization of the funded capacity, adjusting capacity as necessary. Include utilization analysis and NAMTS Program inspections in Fleet Maintenance Activity Assessments of RMCs. c. Provide cost estimates and implementation plans to the Fleet Commanders for proposed additions and deletions to capabilities in Appendix A, as well as increases or decreases to capacity at any and all RMCs. d. Establish policy, requirements and direction for NAMTS program management and execution at RMCs. (1) Provide oversight of NAMTS program execution and qualifications to ensure: (a) Compliance with NAMTS roles, responsibilities and program execution per the NAMTS desk guide, CNRMC M-4700.12. (b) NAMTS enrollment and qualification is maximized. (c) “Hands-on” journeyman-level skills training is an integral part of Job Qualification Requirement (JQR) qualification. (d) The number of experienced JQR journeyman qualified personnel produced, is adequate to fill NAMTS NEC-coded afloat billet requirements established by the cognizant Fleet Commander(s). (2) Provide NAMTS JQR Life Cycle Management including the following: (a) Coordinate with TYCOMs, Surface Warfare Officer’s School - Fleet Enlisted Engineering Training and RMCs to ensure JQRs meet NAMTS NEC requirements. Changes to NAMTS NEC requirements may result from ship system modifications, upgrades or new acquisitions. (b) Develop, review, coordinate feedback or revise JQRs as required. At a minimum, coordinate JQR reviews every three years. (c) Approve new and changes to JQRs. Determine or approve which JQRs are executed at RMCs. (d) For new JQRs, coordinate the development and submission of Course Identification Number packages to support NEC management and training accomplishment. (e) Maintain Master JQR Library. (3) Maintain and monitor a master test question data bank to support pre-and post-JQR examinations and JQR qualification oral boards.

(4) Promote NAMTS program awareness among Fleet activities and sailors, to include: (a) Host and maintain an information web site that supports NAMTS program management and awareness, training materials and metrics. (b) Publish newsletters and other media to enhance program awareness. (c) Establish and maintain a system of metrics to reflect NAMTS program performance including eligibility, enrollment and qualification trends. (5) Establish a manpower and NAMTS NEC At-Sea Requirements Matrix and coordinate periodic reviews with TYCOMs. (a) Develop quarterly review schedules to ensure Ship Manning Documents for all afloat units are reviewed annually at a minimum. (b) In conjunction with manpower reviews, the NAMTS NEC At-Sea Requirements Matrix must be reviewed annually. (c) Review sea and shore rotation impacts resulting from recommended NEC changes. (d) Submit review results and recommendations to United States Fleet Forces or Commander, Pacific Fleet via TYCOMs prior to BCR submissions. 1 NAMTS NEC At-Sea Requirements Matrix changes. 2 NAMTS NEC modifications through the Navy Enlisted Occupational Classification System Board process. 3 Navy Manpower Analysis Center NEC changes. (6) Conduct Quarterly NAMTS Program Reviews with RMC representatives. Reviews must include at a minimum: (a) Eligibility, enrollment, qualification and NECs award trends. (b) Status of manpower, NAMTS NEC At-Sea Requirements Matrix reviews, BCRs, NEC modifications, feedback reports or other pending actions. (7) Develop a series of metrics to measure and monitor the performance and overall health of the NAMTS program. In particular, eligibility, enrollment, qualification and NEC award trends, accounting for all Sailors in NAMTS NEC source ratings, must be measured and analyzed. Metrics must be developed to support both program monitoring within the NAMTS organization and up line reporting as required. e. As MAT Program Manager, establish requirements and guidance for the execution of MATs at the RMCs, including reporting requirements. f. Coordinate with the cognizant TYCOM on the establishment, disestablishment and utilization of MATs. Regional Maintenance Center. a.

RMC areas of responsibility are the same as those identified in Volume II, Part I, Chapter 2, paragraph 2.1.1, Table 2.1 of this manual. The RMC must exercise all I- Level functions and responsibilities when services are required or requested by fleet activities within these areas unless assigned to another RMC by the Fleet Maintenance Officer. This includes utilization of the I-Level capability as appropriate. b. Include details of I-Level capabilities in RMC capability manuals. c. Identify and communicate shop loading to applicable Forces Afloat and TYCOMs to ensure full utilization of the funded capacity. This includes the use of this capacity to establish MATs. d. These requirements apply to Naval Shipyards when they are assigned RMC functions. REGIONAL MAINTENANCE CENTER PERFORMANCE MEASURES. RMC I-Level capability performance will be reported monthly to CNRMC per guidelines in Volume II, Part I, Chapter 4, paragraph 4.6.5.1 of this manual for continuous evaluation. a. MAT utilization and performance measures must be included in the RMC monthly I- Level Reports. b. CNRMC will provide quarterly summary reports of I-Level performance, including MATs, to the cognizant TYCOM and Fleet Maintenance Officer.

VOLUME VI CHAPTER 36 SURFACE FORCE SHIP AND AIRCRAFT CARRIER MODERNIZATION PROCESS REFERENCES. (a) NAVSEA SL720-AA-MAN-030 - Navy Modernization Process Management and Operations Manual (NMP-MOM) (b) COMUSFLTFORCOMINST/COMPACFLTINST 4720.3 - Commander United States Fleet Forces Command (COMUSFLTFORCOM)/Commander Pacific Fleet (COMPACFLT) C5ISR Modernization Policy (c) NAVSEA TS9090-310 – Alterations Accomplished by Alteration Installation Teams (AITs) (d) OPNAVINST 4780.6 – Policy for Acquisition and Management of Service Craft, Combatant Craft, and Boats in the U.S. Navy (e) MARCORSYSCOM 5000.3; SPAWARINST 3058.1; NAVFACINST 5000.15; NAVSUPINST 5000.20; NAVAIRINST 5000.21B; NAVSEAINST 5000.8 - Naval SYSCOM Risk Management Policy (f) NAVSEA TS9090-600 – Ship Installation Drawings (SIDs) (g) NAVSEA TS9090-100 – Liaison Action Records (LARs) SCOPE. This chapter is applicable to all Surface Force ships, Aircraft Carriers, and AEGIS ashore sites involved in the Navy Modernization Process (NMP), as delineated in reference (a). The provisions of this chapter have been developed in collaboration with Naval Operations (OPNAV). Where there are conflicts with reference (a), this chapter must take precedence until such time as OPNAV implementing directives can be modified and issued. Submarine Modernization is described in chapter 3. Exceptions and exemptions to the NMP are identified in reference (a). Reference (b) provides the policy for Command, Control, Communications, Computer, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance modernization.

Reference (c), which is Appendix H of reference (a), governs the policy for Alteration Installation Teams (AIT) installing Ship Changes (SC) including the Regional Maintenance and Modernization Coordination Office (RMMCO) check-in and check-out process. Fleet Commanders (FLTCDR) and Type Commanders (TYCOM), per references (a) through (c), ensure implementation of this process. NOTE: UNAUTHORIZED SHIP CHANGES TO NAVY SHIPS ARE PROHIBITED. PURPOSE. The purpose of this chapter is to provide an overview of the entire NMP. The NMP provides a structure for identifying, planning, designing, approving, installing, sustaining, and maintaining configuration control of ship modernization. The NMP is designed to prevent unauthorized and non-supported SCs from being installed on Navy ships. Unauthorized SCs represent a substantial cost to the Navy in terms of the loss of configuration control, inefficiencies due to unexpected installation interferences, systems and equipment that are not logistically supported, and resources expended to support items which are no longer needed. Unauthorized SCs can also adversely impact the interoperability of highly technical and integrated combat systems which equates to a loss of combat effectiveness due to a reduction in Battle Group and Strike Force Interoperability (SFI) and individual ship capabilities. BACKGROUND. The NMP has progressed from the pre-2004 Fleet Modernization Process to the Ship Maintenance process of 2005-2007 to the NMP of today. The Entitled Process (EP) for Navy Modernization was promulgated by the Commander, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) in 2006 and, upon adoption, became known as the NMP to recognize its broad application and permanence. NAVY MODERNIZATION PROCESS. The NMP employs five modernization phases: Phase I – concept design; Phase II - preliminary design; Phase III - detailed design; Phase IV - advance planning and procurement; and Phase V - installation, check-out and feedback. These phases and the associated policies and processes are documented in reference (a) and in NAVSEA Technical Specifications. Reference (a) also delineates the management roles within the NMP and their respective responsibilities.

The NAVSEA Technical Specifications define policy, process, and responsibilities for specific modernization sub-processes, (e.g., Liaison Action Records (LAR), Ship Installation Drawings (SID), and Alterations Accomplished by AITs). Exceptions and Exemptions. The following exceptions and exemptions apply to the NMP: a. The Deputy Commander for Nuclear Propulsion, , is responsible for all technical matters pertaining to nuclear propulsion of U.S. Navy ships, including all aspects of integration of the nuclear plant into ship systems. The procedures and requirements of this chapter are not applicable to alterations under the cognizance of the Deputy Commander for Nuclear Propulsion. b. Equipage as defined in reference (a). Equipage consists of portable items that are not permanently installed. c. Habitability as delineated in volume VI chapter 16 of this volume. d. Service Craft, Combatant Craft, and Boats as delineated in reference (d). e. Information Assurance and Vulnerability Management (IAVM) products are exempt from this chapter. IAVM is a process that provides positive control of vulnerability notification, corresponding corrective action, and IAVM status visibility for the Department of Defense Network Assets. The IAVM program applies to any device on Department of Defense owned, controlled, or contracted networks. f. Form, Fit, or Function replacement items as defined in reference (a). g. Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy funded installations occurring during new construction. h. Database updates (e.g., threat library updates, technical manual database updates, etc.) are exempt from this chapter. i. Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) Mission Modules (MM) are designed to provide the specific warfighting capabilities and operation for the LCSs. Their flexibility contributes to maritime dominance and provide improved access for the joint force. All MMs designated for embarkation have been authorized via the Mission Package Certification, Warfare Center Certification, Combat System Certification and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) Certification. The MM program will keep the Naval C5IMP Modernization Council (NCMC) apprised of currently certified and fielded Mission Package baselines. Additionally, it will identify plans for fielding newer baselines.

Ao message and Electronic Configuration Control Board (eCCB) Risk Form per reference (b) will be submitted to the FLTCDR for approval prior to embarkation or debarkation on an LCS platform for non-mature MM baselines. Software Policy. NMP requirements for software SCs are determined by their change categories defined in reference (a). The change categories are: a. Major Release. Major releases are not exempt from any NMP requirements. Major releases consist of software that: (1) Contains a noun name not currently fielded. (2) Forces changes in the interface with an external system. (3) Adds, removes, or implements major modification to a capability that was already implemented or intended to be implemented but was not released in a previous version. (4) Requires an on-site installation visit duration including testing, but not training, of greater than 21 calendar days. (5) Impacts functionality inside at least one certification boundary. b. Standard Release. Standard releases are exempt from the Ship Change Document (SCD) review process. Alteration revision records must be created and scheduled in the Navy Data Environment (NDE) Navy Modernization.NET (NM.NET) application for standard releases. Standard releases are additional functionality that does not meet the requirements for a major release and: (1) Corrects implementation of an existing interface with an external system. (2) Offers a change in the interface with an external system. (3) Shifts from one existing interface to another. (4) Adds or removes implemented functionality. (5) Has a training and, or operational impact that is noticeable to the user and can be informed by Fleet Advisory or electronic notification upon install. (6) Has an operational impact that increases administrator or operator workload by no more than 20%. (7) Requires an on-site installation. (8) Are other impactful non-hardware changes to the hosting environment. c. Minor Release. Minor releases are any other software change that does not meet the criteria for a major or standard release. Minor releases include Inconsequential Overmatch Software Armory software deliveries. Minor releases are exempt from the NMP. NOTE:

SHIP’S FORCE MUST NOT BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ACCOMPLISHING RE-LOADS. d. Restorative (Re-Load) Installation. Restorative installations are re-loads of previously installed software version on a newly installed hardware component, system, or operating system. New alteration accomplishment records must be created and scheduled in NDE NM.NET application for Restorative Installations. When an AIT needs to come onboard to accomplish the re-load and subsequent testing, the requirements of references (a) and (b) apply. e. Qualified Development Security Operations (DevSecOps) Deployments. Qualified DevSecOps Deployments (QDD) are any functions, capabilities or fleet driven updates that are delivered over the network using a qualified DevSecOps Framework. QDDs are exempt from the SCD review process. Alteration records must be created NM.NET to capture QDD installations. QDDs are also exempt from the Target Configuration Date (TCD) Waiver process defined in reference (b). SHIP CHANGE DOCUMENTS. The SCD is the mechanism used to communicate and obtain approval for planned modernization. SCDs are initiated in the NDE EP application, are submitted through a structured review process, and ensure that applicable Navy stakeholders review and approve the proposed SCs prior to installation or execution. Scope. SCD scope consists of the following categories: a. Ship Modifications. Ship Modifications consist of Ship Alteration and Alteration Equivalent to Repair Alteration Types. b. Internal Equipment Modifications. Internal equipment modifications consist of Engineering Changes, Machinery Alterations, Ordnance Alterations, and Software Deliveries, as well as QDD Alteration Types. c. Site Modifications. Site modifications are installations to shore sites. Funding. SCD Funding comes from the following sources: a. Program Funded. Funded for installation by a System Command (SYSCOM) or Program Executive Office. b. Fleet Funded. Funded for installation by the Fleet. c. Non-Navy Funded. Funding from non-Navy sources (e.g., Missile Defense Agency). Duration. SCD Duration consists of the following types: a. Permanent Changes.

Permanent changes are modifications of ships and their systems that are not temporary in nature. A permanent SC may include a prototype installation to support development and operational testing. b. Non-Permanent Changes. Non-Permanent Changes (NPC) are SCs that will be installed on a temporary basis for Test & Evaluation purposes or to demonstrate a new or improved capability for the Fleet. NPCs are intended to be installed for one operational deployment and may not exceed one year in duration. NOTE: NON-PERMANENT CHANGES WILL BE REMOVED WITHIN 1 YEAR FROM INSTALLTION UNLESS A WAIVER IS APPROVED BY THE FLTCDR OR TYCOM FOR AN EXTENDED EVALUATION PERIOD. Non-Standard. Non-Standard SCDs address unique circumstances. Non-Standard SCDs are subject to additional or streamlined requirements. Mandatory Safety. A SC to correct or mitigate a Serious or High System Safety Risk as defined in reference (e). It may also be a SC directed as the result of a Safety Investigation Board or Naval Safety Center as an action in response to a Class A mishap or as determined by formal Flag level direction. Fielding Plan (FP) changes to Mandatory Safety SCDs require a full SCD review cycle to ensure Technical Warrant Holder concurrence and approval from the Ship Program Manager (SPM), TYCOM, and resource sponsor. The deferral or cancellation, after any Decision Point of SCDs designated as Mandatory Safety, requires reevaluation for changes in mitigation strategy or residual risk acceptance of those changes. This review and approval will take place through the SCD review cycle. Fleet Experimentation and Technology Demonstration. Fleet Experimentation (FLEX) SCs consist of experimentation requiring the services of fleet assets during exercises such as Trident Warrior. Experiments are supported by data collection and analysis, providing tangible products for Fleet use, and will provide resultant findings and recommendations leading to improvements in naval warfighting capabilities spanning Doctrine, Organization, Training, Materiel, Leadership Development, Personnel, Facilities, and Policy.

A Technology Demonstration (TECH DEMO) is a system, equipment, capability demonstration to evaluate a system, principal unit or software and, or integrate with the required interfacing Naval systems. FLEX or TECH DEMO SCDs must adhere to the following conditions: a. The duration of installations should not exceed 90 days including removal and restoration. b. FLEX or TECH DEMO SCs can be accomplished in port or at-sea. c. FLEX or TECH DEMO SCs cannot be used to provide an interim capability to support operational and training requirements for Platform TYCOMs, Operational Commanders, Immediate Superior In Command (ISIC), or Commander, US Fleet Forces Command (USFFC). d. The FLEX or TECH DEMO SC installations must be removed at the end of the experiment, the ship(s) returned to the original configuration or state, and the original system recertified. Emergent. Emergent SCDs are those items that require immediate installation (within 45 days or less of the first identification of the requirement) and, or reprioritization of tasking and reallocation of resources to support accelerated development and installation. Emergent SCs must meet the criteria defined in reference (a). The Participating Acquisition Resource Manager (PARM) or designated representative will issue an emergent change request message to the appropriate installation approval authority. The installation approval authority reviews and approves or disapproves the emergent change requirement via Naval Message. The approval authorities for SFI Category (CAT) 1 or 2 SCs is the FLTCDR and the Platform TYCOM for SFI CAT 3 or 4 SCs. Modernization Through Attrition And Modernization In Lieu of Repair. Modernization Through Attrition Modernization In Lieu of Repair (MTA/MILR) SCDs are SCs used to facilitate Condition Based Maintenance. Approval is based on the same criteria as any SC and installation will be determined by the TYCOM during the execution year. MTA/MILR actions are changes to components, or systems executed on an “as fails” basis or Condition Based Maintenance criteria.

MTA/MILR actions targeted for a ship class, but without a known ship-specific FP, may be required to enhance maintainability, resolve hardware or software obsolescence, or to address declining Intermediate or Depot level repair resources. MTA actions may not impact shipboard or interfacing systems, certifications and do not result in additional operational capability. Low Impact. Low Impact Internal Equipment Modifications are modernization or sustainment SCs which do not have a significant impact on Chief of Naval Operations (CNO) and Maintenance availabilities. Low impact ship changes can be authorized for CNO availabilities with condensed milestones. SHIP CHANGE DOCUMENT PROCESS. The following paragraphs outline the SCD Process. Ship Change Document Initiation. SCDs can be initiated at Phase I, II, or III. The initiator will coordinate with the SCD submitter to determine the entry phase based on the maturity level of the SC. SCDs should be initiated in the NDE EP application. The initiator will fill out the mandatory fields of the SCD at a minimum, including identification of the submitter responsible for the SCD and then submit to the SCD submitter for review. NOTE: UPON IDENTIFICATION OF POTENTIAL SYSTEM OR EQUIPMENT IMPROVEMENT BY THE SHIP, SHIP’S FORCE PERSONNEL WILL FORWARD SC REQUESTS TO THE ISIC. THE ISIC WILL ENDORSE AND FORWARD THE REQUEST TO THE RESPECTIVE TYCOM FOR SCD INITIATION. Ship Change Document Submission. The submitter should review and agree with the need for the change, the high-level proposed resolution and proposed FP prior to submitting the SCD for review by the Technical Assessment Team (TAT). Technical Assessment Team Review. The TAT consists of SYSCOM and Program Executive Office technical personnel who review the SCD to ensure the SCD is technically feasible and to identify any ship integration issues that may impact its overall benefit to the Fleet. Upon completion of the TAT Review, the SCD will be forwarded to the SPM. Ship Program Manager Review. The SPM will review the results of the TAT Review and provide an overall recommendation to the Decision Board.

Upon completion of the SPM Review, the SCD will be forwarded into Cost Benefit Analysis (CBA) Review. Cost Benefit Assessment Review. The CBA Change Manager coordinates the review of the CBA which includes the FP. The CBA Change Manager should review the results of the CBA review and determine if the CBA is complete and accurate prior to forwarding to the resource sponsor. Resource Sponsor Review. The SCD should be forwarded to the applicable Office of the Chief of Naval Operations (OPNAV) resource sponsor for review. The resource sponsor will review the funding information in the CBA and determine if there is funding available and provide additional comments. Upon completion of resource sponsor review, the SCD is forwarded to the applicable NMP Decision Board for review and vote. Ship Change Document Voting. SCD voters consist of the TYCOM, SPM, OPNAV Resource Sponsor of Record, FLTCDR, and, or OPNAV N83 (SCDs utilizing maintenance funds). The applicable Decision Boards are determined by the total cost of the SCD. The three hierarchical Decision Boards are O-6, 1 and 2 Star, and 3 Star. Navy Modernization Process Phases. The following subparagraphs describe the phases of the NMP. Phase I. The purpose of beginning in Phase I is to document a need for change, propose a resolution, or gain approval to proceed with development of that resolution into an engineered SC. Phase II. The purpose of this phase is to perform preliminary design development of the SC, document results of the preliminary design, and gain approval to continue to Phase III (detailed design). Included in preliminary design development can be selection of technologies, establishment of design parameters, and prototype development. Phase II is also utilized to document the design of Prototypes, FLEX, TECH DEMOs, and NPCs which are authorized for installation upon Phase II approval. Phase II(a). Phase II(a) combines Phases II and III and is appropriate for internal equipment modifications that meet the criteria in reference (a). Phase II(a) will allow early visibility of the change, via Phase I submission, while "bypassing" Phase II.

A SCD can utilize the Phase II(a) process only upon request in Phase I with TAT concurrence. Phase II(a) results in a Decision Point (DP) 3 decision. Phase III. The purpose of Phase III is to document detailed design development of the SC. The technical documentation provided with an SCD to support DP3 must include the level of detail sufficient to support a critical design review. DP3 provides authority to procure, test, and mature the SC. Phase IV. The purpose of Phase IV is to accomplish ship and site-specific advanced planning and achieve maturity of the SC. The attention is redirected from overall SC design to specific requirements for installation on a specific ship or site. This phase includes availability work package integration, finalized ship or site design (including ship check, site survey and development of drawings, technical installation instructions, etc.), initiation of procurement, and installation readiness reviews. Fielding Plans. When an SCD is initiated at any phase, the Submitter will provide a FP using the CBA Installation FP Tab that reflects the planned number of units, by ship or site, per Fiscal Year. Once the FP change has been approved in NDE-EP, ship-specific installation information will be scheduled by the PARM in Navy Data Environment-Navy Modernization (NDE-NM). The PARM and submitter must coordinate data entry to ensure that the applicable ships or sites and the total number of production units (e.g., quantity per Fiscal Year in the CBA) match the ships or sites numbers scheduled in NDE-NM at each DP and reflects any changes. Ship Change Scheduling. SC Scheduling provides visibility to authorization activities for inclusion into the SPM or TYCOM authorization documents. SC Scheduling in NDE NM.NET must match the approved SCD FP. a. Incremented Ship Change s. An increment of an SC is a finite, definable, bounded portion of the total scope of work required to fully accomplish a single SC. Increments are not to denote different versions of the same hardware or software system.

If it is known during the development of an SCD that incremental installation is necessary and appropriate, the increments will be fully defined as part of the Description of Change and evaluated during the TAT review of the SCD. b. If it is necessary to increment the installation post DP3 and before Start of Installation for the affected ship, a LAR approved by the SPM can be utilized to define the scope of each increment. The PARM should update the FP after approval of the LAR to show the newly defined increments and submit the revised SCD for approval via the DP Boards. The LAR should be attached to the SCD as a permanent record of the incremental decision. In cases when SID development has started, a LAR is required to the Planning Yard (PY) to identify changes required to the SIDs. c. To increment an SC after the Start of Installation during a maintenance availability and the remaining production work needs to be scheduled in a subsequent CNO availability, an informational Electronic LAR (eLAR) should be developed by the PARM to define the scope of each increment for the affected ship. The eLAR should be attached to the SCD, SCD updated (including FP change), and forwarded to the NMP DB for approval. The PARM should update NDE-EP, NDE-NM, and NDE Afloat Master Planning System (AMPS) modules after approval of the eLAR to show the newly defined increments for the affected ship(s). The PARM has the responsibility to take all appropriate actions to address all increments including coordination with the PY to address SIDs for each increment, RMMCO to address status of the increments in RMMCO.NET, SPM to address status of ILS certification, and C5IMP stakeholders to address impacts to the baseline. d. Some incremented installs may also require a Departure from Specification (DFS) to document the resulting ship’s condition based on the incrementation. In those cases, the PARM should be responsible for generating the required DFS. Ship Change Planning. The PARM should plan to accomplish all maturity requirements and modernization milestones paragraph below.

The PARM should ensure all technical documentation is complete; all material has been procured and is available for installation; pre-installation testing has been accomplished per the appropriate installation and testing plans; all conjunctive SCs are either installed or mature; all certifications and qualifications have been completed. a. Ship Installation Drawings. Drawings, change instructions, material procurement and logistics required for SC installation will be developed or accomplished as necessary utilizing internal processes. If the scope of the SC affects only internals to the equipment, SIDs are not required. Equipment level drawings will be developed to ensure that all technical requirements are identified. SIDs should be accomplished per reference (f). The PARM should task and fund ship checks and SID development per milestones paragraph below. SID approval is delegated by the SPM to the PY. Installation Control Drawings and Installation Requirements Drawings are used to provide supplemental guidance in support of SID development per reference (f). b. Liaison Action Records. LARs are the formal documentation tool for communication among Availability Planning Activities, PYs, SUPSHIPs, Executing Yards, SYSCOMs, PARMs, AITs, SPMs, In Service Engineering Agents (ISEAs), and other organizations involved in planning and executing ship modernization. LARs should be used to facilitate the resolution of design questions and change requests regarding drawings, technical documentation, and tasking assignments; requirements for departures; identification of increments not specified at the time of SC approval; and transmittal of drawings for approval or archiving. Policy for LARs is defined in reference (g). c. Milestones. SC maturity and availability contractual requirements are subject to planning milestones to ensure timely planning and execution of availabilities. Enterprise specific milestones are identified in reference (a), formal SPM correspondence (e.g., Naval Messages, Memorandums, etc.) and volume II, part II, chapter 2 (Appendices D and E) of this manual.

Failure to comply with JFMM volume II part II chapter 2 of this manual can result in deferral of a SC from SPM or TYCOM authorization documentation or additional requirements to be added or remain on a SPM Letter of Authorization (LOA) or TYCOM authorization documentation (e.g., Risk Assessment Approval, Late Add Approval, etc.). d. Certifications and Qualifications. All required certifications and qualifications should be documented in the SCD and accomplished prior to installation. Certifications include, but are not limited to: (1) Warfare System or Element (System) level Certifications (2) Warfare System Installation Assessment (3) ILS Certification (4) Application Integration Certification (5) Cybersecurity Accreditation and Certification (6) Weapons Systems Explosive Safety Review Board non-firing concurrence for installation (7) Electromagnetic Interference Impact Assessment and System Electromagnetic Capability Certification (8) Shock Qualification or Submitted Shock Deficiency Plan e. Fleet Commander C5I Baseline. The C5I Modernization Process is governed by reference (b). All SCs with a SFI CAT of 1 or 2 require authorization in the FLTCDR C5I Baseline. Authorization in the FLTCDR C5I baseline is critical maturity requirement for SPM or TYCOM authorization. SFI CAT determinations are made during SCD TAT Reviews. (1) SCs can be added to the FLTCDR C5I Baseline through two different methods. SCs that are scheduled prior to the Baseline Lock Event (BLE) for a ship will be reviewed at the BLE and the FLTCDR will determine if the SC is authorized, planned not authorized, or will not be included in the baseline. Any SCs that were not added to the baseline during the BLE will require the PARM submission of an eCCB Risk Form and FLTCDR approval. (2) Any SCs being removed from the baseline after BLE will require PARM submission of an electronic Removal eCCB Removal Risk Form and FLTCDR approval. Depending on the SC maturity and scheduling timeframe, Risk Assessment Requests and TCD Waivers may be required. f. Risk Assessments.

SCs that are immature require an approved Risk Assessment Request to remain on the SPM LOA after the LOA Late Add milestone in reference (a). Additionally, if a SC is scheduled after the Late Add milestone and immature, an approved Risk Assessment Request, in addition to a Late Add message, is required to be added to the SPM LOA. Immature SCs scheduled outside of CNO availabilities will require an approved Risk Assessment Request for FLTCDR or TYCOM authorization. Risk Assessment Requests are submitted to the FLTCDR or TYCOM per the Ao message templates in reference (b). FLTCDR approval is required for SFI Category I and II SCs, and TYCOM approval is required for SFI CAT III and IV SCs. g. Target Configuration Date Waivers. The TCD is established by the FLTCDR for each ship to minimize configuration changes during the Basic, Integrated, Advanced, and Sustainment phases. Changes to the C5I baseline outside the Modernization Window adversely affect an operational unit’s ability to train, and therefore, require TCD Waiver approval from the appropriate FLTCDR. TCD Waiver requests must be submitted for any SFI CAT I, II, or III SCs per reference (b). h. Late Adds. SCs that are not authorized for a CNO Availability prior to the Enterprise specific LOA Late Add milestones paragraph above will require Late Add approval. Depending on the Enterprise, Late Add milestones may vary based on SC scope and impact to the availability. Late Add requests must be submitted by the cognizant PARM. The TYCOM is the activity responsible for reviewing and approval or disapproval of Late Add requests. Ship Program Manager or TYCOM Authorization. SPMs and TYCOMs are the activities responsible for reviewing SC maturity and authorizing SCs for installation. a. Ship Program Manager or TYCOM Authorization (CNO Availabilities). The SPM (Program Alterations) and TYCOM (Fleet Alterations) will evaluate the maturity of each SC scheduled to occur in a CNO Availability based on their Enterprise specific processes, using the Installation Readiness Assessment, per the applicable milestones.

The SPM or TYCOM will document the decision to authorize or defer each individual SC via a LOA or a LOA Change message. Any SC that is not mature per the milestones will require Risk Assessment Request approval from the FLTCDR or TYCOM. Any SC that is not authorized in accordance with the LOA milestones will require an approved Late Add request. b. Type Commander Authorization (Outside CNO Availabilities). The TYCOM will evaluate the maturity of each SC scheduled outside of a CNO Availability. Any SC that is immature requires Risk Assessment Request approval from the FLTCDR or TYCOM. For Carriers, SCs identified in the Modernization Readiness Assessment as mature are authorized for installation. For Surface Force Ships, the TYCOM will document authorized SCs via a Quarterly Installation Scheduling Message. Pre-Installation Check-Out. Pre-Installation Check-Out (PICO) is a test designed to evaluate and baseline the operational status and performance of the equipment, systems, and interfaces. PICO completion is of vital importance to both the maintenance and modernization communities to ensure corrective actions and responsibility for discrepancy resolution is effectively and timely identified and completed. PICO must be conducted for all scheduled modernization installations during CNO availabilities when SCs or alterations modify or relocate existing equipment or systems, including modifications that affect existing interfaces between systems. The purpose is to identify pre-existing discrepancies, which if uncorrected, could delay or prevent the successful completion of the SC. The PARM or ISEA will ensure that PICO testing requirements are submitted to the coordinating activity per the Enterprise specific coordination method identified in references (a) and (c). Regardless of coordination method, all required PICO(s) will be targeted for completion 90 to 30 days prior to the Start of Availability based on the ship’s operational schedule. For installations accomplished outside of CNO Availabilities, PARMs or ISEAs will coordinate with TYCOMs to accomplish the PICO. a.

For all installations (AIT and Non-AIT), Ship’s Force will ensure discrepancies are documented in the ship’s Current Ship Maintenance Project (CSMP) and coordinate new work with the Naval Supervisory Authority (NSA) and Lead Maintenance Activity (LMA). b. The PARM or ISEA will provide a draft PICO Completion Naval Message using the suggested format in reference (c). All PICO discrepancies will have a Ship’s Force CSMP entry, assigned Job Control Number, and be included in the PICO Completion Naval Message. Ship’s Force will review and release the PICO Completion Naval Message. Ship’s Force will continue to track CSMP items identified during the PICO and coordinate required maintenance actions (e.g., equipment repair and parts requisition) to support post installation testing. In the event a PICO can’t be accomplished or completed, the PARM or ISEA will document via a Naval Message. NOTE: THE AIT INSTALLATION COORDINATOR SHOULD BRIEF THE PICO STATUS AT THE SHIP’S IN-BRIEF PRIOR TO START OF INSTALLTION. SHIP’S FORCE WILL PROVIDE STATUS OF PICO DISCREPANCIES UNDER THEIR COGNIZANCE. Phase V. The purpose of Phase V is to execute the SC and document completion and delivery of all installation requirements. SCs must be authorized in Phase IV to proceed to installation phase (Phase V). Once all planned installations for applicable ships have been completed and documented in NDE, the SCD is closed out. Regional Maintenance and Modernization Coordination Office. RMMCO is a regionally aligned organization that serves as the initial control point for all waterfront-related SC installations performed by AITs per reference (c). The RMMCO Gatekeeper is designated by the NSA or Ship Acquisition Program Manager for New Construction ships. The RMMCO AIT Check-In process provides the AIT Manager and AIT On-Site Installation Coordinator (OSIC) with a tool to initiate the check-in procedures required for the installation of an SC aboard ships. NOTE: AITS SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED ONBOARD ANY SHIP TO ACCOMPLISH INSTALLATION WITHOUT RMMCO AND NSA CHECK-IN AUTHORIZATIONS.

IF AN UNAUTHORIZED AIT IS IDENTIFIED, SHIP’S FORCE SHOULD NOTIFY THE NSA. Electronic Submission. The AIT Manager will submit an electronic RMMCO Form for each SC to the RMMCO Gatekeeper. RMMCO Gatekeepers will pre-screen the RMMCO Form and provide feedback on any discrepancies. Regional Maintenance and Modernization Coordination Office Check-In. The AIT Manager, OSIC and AIT Lead must check-in with RMMCO prior to reporting to the ship. During check-in, RMMCO will review SC authorization and maturity documentation provided by the AIT Manager, OSIC and AIT Lead. All discrepancies identified during Electronic Submission must be addressed prior to RMMCO Check-In. RMMCO will require the following documentation for RMMCO Check-In: a. AIT Quality Assurance (QA) Workbook. b. Copy of ILS Certification or FLTCDR or TYCOM approved Risk Assessment c. Copy of approved Platform System Operational Verification Test (SOVT) or Test Procedure (TP) Naval Supervisory Authority Check-In. The AIT OSIC and AIT Lead will check-in with the NSA for review of logistics, Environmental, Safety & Occupational Health, and QA requirements. NSA Check-In will consist of the following: a. NSA logistics representatives will review the most recent approved ILS certification. b. The Environmental, Safety & Occupational Health representatives will review the following documents: fire safety plan, list of AIT personnel that have taken the NSA safety course (in-person) within the last year, permission to paint (if required), permission to use solvents and adhesives (if required), and list of Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) (if applicable). c. The QA representatives will review the AIT QA Workbook. The AIT QA Workbook is not required for stand-alone software only changes unless directed by the AIT Manager. d. Once the AIT installation package is verified, the RMMCO Check-In or Check-Out Form will be printed by RMMCO or the NSA and provided to the AIT. This form identifies all items that will require signature verification of accomplishment and, or receipt of the list of ILS deliverables.

Alteration Installation Teams Ship’s In-Brief. The purpose of the AIT Ship’s In-Brief is to provide an overview of the SC per reference (c). Additionally, the in-brief should consist of the following: a. PICO Status Review b. Work to be Accomplished c. Schedule of Key Events and Milestones d. Planned Ship’s Evolutions e. Impact of Support Services f. AIT OSIC and Ship’s Force Responsibilities g. Conjunctive SCs h. SOVT or TP i. ILS and Training to be Provided j. Points of Contact In-Brief Scheduling. The in-brief should be scheduled and coordinated by the AIT OSIC. It should be conducted after RMMCO Check-In and prior to the initiation of SC accomplishment. The following personnel should be invited to attend the in-brief (as applicable): a. Commanding Officer, Executive Officer, Ship’s Availability Manager, applicable Department Heads, Division Officers, Supply Officer, and Technical Personnel, Operator Personnel (i.e., Fire Controlman [FC], Electronic Technician [ET], Operations Specialist [OS], etc.). b. TYCOM, Squadron, NSA, LMA, Shipyard Trades Personnel (i.e., FC, ET, OS, etc.). c. The AIT OSIC may invite ISEA representatives or other Subject Matter Experts to support the in-brief. WORK EXECUTION. Production Work. The designated Executing Activity will execute the work based on the technical documentation developed during Phase IV. The NSA is responsible for government oversight of all work performed during an availability. For SCs accomplished by AITs, the AIT OSIC, assigned by the AIT Manager, is responsible for overseeing contractor work and should work closely with the NSA to ensure the proper integration and installation of the SC. Plan of Action and Milestones Requirements. The following is guidance for AIT Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) and weekly progress updates during CNO and non-CNO availabilities per reference (c). Notional Plan of Action and Milestones during CNO Availabilities.

Notional POA&Ms (sometimes referred to as Preliminary POA&Ms) are provided during Phase IV. Notional POA&Ms are used to support advance planning scheduling and duration analysis for Surface Force Ships and initial integration to support the development of the Integrated Master Schedule or Integrated Production Schedule for Aircraft Carriers. Production Plan of Action and Milestones during CNO Availabilities. Production POA&Ms must be provided by the AIT Manager to develop or update the Integrated Master Schedule or Integrated Production Schedule. All activities must comply with Key Event schedules promulgated by the NSA and LMA. To streamline and standardize AIT deliverable documents, AIT Production POA&M submissions must contain data elements specified in NAVSEA SI 009-60, using the format in reference (c). Plan of Action and Milestones during Non-CNO Availabilities. POA&Ms will be provided per reference (c). Weekly Progress Updates. The NSA or LMA will require the AIT OSIC or AIT Lead to participate in routine and special progress meetings for the purpose of work coordination and progress reviews. Unless changes occurred to the SC or testing schedule, updates are not required until the production work has reached its planned start date. AITs are responsible for complying with the reporting requirements of NAVSEA Standard Items 009-60 or 009-111 for updated production schedules and progress reporting through weekly progress updates. Any changes to the work schedule provided via Weekly POA&M progress updates should be reported to the NSA, LMA, and Ship’s designated point of contact as soon as changes are identified. NOTE: SOVTS AND TPS SHOULD NOT BE SIGNED IF THE CAPABILITY TO BE DELIVERED HAS NOT BEEN SATISFACTORILY DEMONSTRATED OR THE SYSTEM IS NOT CYBER COMPLIANT. NOTE: SOVT OR TP SIGNATORY APPROVALS SHOULD NOT BE WITHELD FOR CAPABILITIES OUTSIDE THE SCOPE OF THE SC OR ISSUES WITH PRIOR VERSIONS OF THE SYSTEM AND SOFTWARE. SYSTEM OPERATIONAL VERIFICATION TEST AND TEST PROCEDURE.

SOVTs and TPs are formal processes used to verify the installed system, and equipment that has been completed per applicable requirements including any interface with external systems or equipment and any systems or equipment that was temporarily moved or disconnected to accomplish the install. SOVTs and TPs can vary in scope, other than a full system test, if boundaries for the test are clearly defined and invoked to validate the modification or install. It can be a single test or a battery of tests that verifies the installed or modified component(s), equipment, systems, interfaces with existing systems, and systems impacted by the installation are properly installed and operates as intended at the platform specific requirement and environment. SOVT and TP format and requirements are contained in reference (a). The SOVT or TP will be conducted for all equipment directly impacted by accomplishment of the SC. A completed SOVT or TP is defined as an executed SOVT or TP document that has been witnessed and signed by Ship’s Force, with all test results, system configuration details, and any discrepancies recorded or uploaded into the appropriate data repository. The SOVT or TP discrepancy list should be provided to the NSA. The OSIC, AIT Manager or ISEA will provide a complete set of test reports to Ship’s Force and the NSA at the completion of the SC testing. INTEGRATED LOGISTICS SUPPORT. Integrated Logistics Support Product Delivery. The AIT OSIC is responsible for delivery of all ILS products, as outlined in the ILS Certification. The AIT OSIC should obtain required signatures verifying delivery and noting any ILS deficiencies. The AIT OSIC is responsible for providing an itemized inventory utilizing the form DD 1149 (if applicable) for all deliverables to the ship with a signature from the appropriate department head or authorized personnel. ILS Products Delivery will be tracked by the NSA’s designated representative. For Surface Force Ships, the Regional Maintenance Center (RMC) or Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) has assumed the NSA’s ILS functions, and ILS products may be delivered to the Ship by the AIT or NSA or FLC as appropriate.

For Aircraft Carrier availabilities conducted in Naval Shipyards, the shipyard has assumed the NSA’s ILS function, and in private a shipyard, the resident Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Conversion and Repair performs the NSA’s functions; all ILS products must be delivered to the Maintenance Support Center (MSC). Accordingly, the NSA, Regional Maintenance Center or FLC are responsible for verifying that all ILS products have been delivered to support the installation of a SC and ensuring all ILS products are available as needed for SC installation and check-out of systems and equipment. Ship Installation Drawings Red-Lines. The AIT Manager will ensure that SID Red-Line mark-ups of all PY approved drawings for the SC, including all LARs, deviations, and variances approved by the PY, are provided to indicate the actual “as installed” configuration on the ship. Delivery of the final SID Red-Lines are required to the ship and PY no later than 30 days after the Ship’s Force or NSA Out-Brief. NOTE: FOR THOSE SHIP CHANGES NOT FULLY COMPLETE, ENSURE THE OUTSTANDING ITEMS ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE NSA COMPLETION MESSAGE AND, OR THE COMPLETION REPORT NAVAL MESSAGE. ADDITIONALLY, IF PRODUCTION IS INCOMPLETE, SOVT OR TP IS NOT STARTED OR COMPLETED, OR ALL ILS DELIVERABLES ARE NOT PROVIDED, THE OSIC SHOULD PROVIDE THE CURRENT SYSTEM AND EQUIPMENT STATUS AT THE OUT-BRIEF. IN THESE CASES, COMMUNICATION WITH THE RMMCO IS STILL REQUIRED. COMPLETION. Ship’s Force or NSA Out-Brief. The Ship’s Force or NSA outbrief should be scheduled and coordinated by the AIT OSIC for all SCs per reference (c). The TYCOM, NSA, LMA, NAVSEA 21 Phased Maintenance Representative, Ship’s Force, and PY On-Site Logistics Representatives should be invited to attend all outbriefs. The outbrief should be conducted after completion of the SC and prior to RMMCO Check-Out.

Normally, the AIT OSIC will obtain the required Ship’s Force and NSA verification signatures per reference (c) on the Alteration Completion Report at the outbrief. Completion Report Naval Message. The AIT OSIC should provide a draft copy of the Completion Report Naval Message. The message should be reviewed and released by Ship’s Force within seven days of the outbrief. In addition to the ACR and Completion Report Naval Message, the status and timeline for completion of the following items will be addressed during the outbrief, if applicable: a. SOVT or TP b. Ship’s Force training completion c. ILS delivery d. Configuration Data Manager’s Database – Open Architecture (CDMD-OA) or Model Based Product Support (MBPS) final configuration data e. SID Red-Lines Regional Maintenance and Modernization Coordination Office Check-Out. After the SC completion and outbrief, the AIT OSIC or AIT Lead must check-out with RMMCO with the following documents: a. Completed and signed RMMCO Form b. Signed Training Verification Report (if applicable) c. SOVT or TP cover sheet(s), discrepancy sheet and signature sheet d. Signed form DD 1149 (if applicable) NOTE: THE RMMCO FORM SHOULD NOT BE CLOSED OUT IF SHIP’S FORCE DOES NOT SIGN THE SOVT OR TP DUE TO DISCREPANCIES. Ship Changes Completion Status Update. The PARM should set the accomplishment status code to a completion status and record the completion date for all completed SC accomplishments in the NM.NET application per reference (a). Ship Change Document Closeout. Upon final planned installation completion, the SCD should be reviewed by the Submitter to ensure all planned installations are complete and confirm that all ILS has been delivered for all installations. Once this is accomplished, the SCD may be considered complete.

VOLUME VI CHAPTER 37 REGIONAL MAINTENANCE CENTER PASSIVE COUNTERMEASURE SYSTEM SUPPORT REQUIREMENTS REFERENCES. (a) OPNAVINST 9070.2 - Signature Control Policy for Ships and Craft of the U.S. Navy (b) NAVSEA RMC CERT 05P1 - Passive Countermeasure System (PCMS) Waterfront Support Certification Plan (c) NAVSEA SE400-DA-MMO-010 - Passive Countermeasure System (PCMS) Technical Manual (d) Maintenance Index Page 4721/081 - CG/DDG/LPD Passive Countermeasure System (PCMS) (e) NAVSEA RIM 05P1 - PCMS Repair and Installation Methods (f) NAVSEA ACD 05P1 - PCMS Access, Material Control and Disposal Manual (g) Maintenance Index Page 4721/082 - CVN Passive Countermeasure System (PCMS) (h) NAVSEA RIM (SLT) 05P1 - PCMS Repair and Installation methods for Type 3R SLT (i) NAVSEA ACD/J 05P1 - PCMS Access, Material Control and Disposal Manual (Japan) (j) NAVSEA ACD/R 05P1 - PCMS Access, Material Control and Disposal Manual (Rota) (k) NAVSEA ACD (CVN) 05P1 - PCMS Access, Material Control and Disposal Manual (CVN) PURPOSE. Per references (a) through (k), to provide guidance in the execution of a shore based Passive Countermeasure System (PCMS) maintenance program in the U.S. Surface Fleets. Waterfront support for the PCMS is focused through the homeport Regional Maintenance Center (RMC). To support the Fleet PCMS program each RMC must be capable of conducting the following core PCMS activities: a. PCMS Readiness Improvement Program (RIP). b. PCMS Maintainer and Supervisor technical training. c. Installation and removal of Motion Measurement System. d. AP-1 and AP-2 system assessments. AP-2 is not applicable to CVN. e. Technical assists. f.

Prioritization and quality assurance of all topside PCMS work related to or impacting PCMS resources and procedures. Requirements for these tasks are identified in reference (b). A general system description is provided in reference (c). g. Support of a RMC Production Repair Replace Facility. This facility will be outfitted and stocked by the RMC for accomplishment of tiling on ship items which have been removed from or are destined for PCMS ships. The facility must include, at minimum, an on-site RMC technician, certified by the NAVSEA Technical Warrant Holder at Waterfront Level 2 Maintainer Instructor, to act as supervisor and manager of the production shop. The designated Code 900 production shop manager must coordinate training and oversight with PCMS SME (Code 200) at the RMC as needed. This capability will be RMC funded stocking of necessary tools, consumables and tiles such that work performed at the shop will not require specific ship provided materials or funding. PASSIVE COUNTERMEASURE SYSTEM EVENT DESCRIPTION. a. PCMS RIP. RIPs are scheduled by the Type Commander (TYCOM) via the Immediate Superiors In Command (ISIC). ISICs obtain primary and secondary dates, submit via action to TYCOM with information to the local RMC. This weeklong event is designed to provide on board training to the entire ship PCMS team, focused on maintenance and inspection training. Curricula are available for both the PCMS maintenance person and PCMS supervisor personnel. The RIP focuses on one day of classroom training, followed by shipboard training that includes assessment and repairs training to the system (trim, caulk, application of material, etc.). This is the primary method of delivering training and PCMS certification for Ship’s Force personnel for CG/DDG/LPD. It also serves the purpose of providing a focused period for accomplishment of a prioritized selection of Ship’s Force capable maintenance. Stand-alone onboard technical training (PCMS Supervisor or Maintainer) may be provided to ships CVN/CG/DDG/LPD) if delivering that training via the RIP process is not possible. This form of training can be requested by the ship directly through the local RMC PCMS SME.

This training is requested through the RMC by ship submission of a 2K. b. Motion Measurement System. Per references (d), ships without installed telemetry equipment require installation and removal of Motion Measurement System for radar cross-section testing. This is accomplished by the RMC following ship submission of a 4790/2K request. c. AP-1 and AP-2 (CG/DDG/LPD) assessments. These comprise the annual Subject Matter Expert (SME) assessment of the ship system. It utilizes a visual assessment process in order to provide a prioritized maintenance plan for the ship. This complements the ship’s measurement. A structured discipline is used for this assessment. d. Technical assistance. RMC SMEs are responsible for responding to Forces Afloat requests for PCMS technical assistance. The RMC technician must be certified by the NAVSEA Technical Warrant Holder at a minimum for Level 2 Maintainer Instruction, to directly assist the ship in identifying and organizing a Ship’s Force PCMS maintenance project. The technician would provide on-site advice and quality assurance assistance. e. Prioritization and Quality Assurance of I and D Level Work. RMC SMEs must be utilized by the RMCs to provide technical advice, including work prioritization, and quality assurance of all I and D Level PCMS related or PCMS impacting work executed under the purview of the RMC. PASSIVE COUNTERMEASURE SYSTEM PERSONNEL CERTIFICATION. Passive Countermeasure System In-Service Engineering Activity. The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) Topside Signatures Technical Warrant Holder has assigned Naval Surface Warfare Center Port Hueneme Detachment (NSWC PHD) as the PCMS In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA). The Technical Warrant Holder (NAVSEA 05P1) retains final authority for all PCMS personnel certification. Support Personnel. Per reference (b), PCMS personnel certification is required every three years. Qualifications for PCMS certification are successful completion of NAVSEA sponsored PCMS installation course conducted under the authority of NSWC PHD (S22) and on-the-job-training witnessed by a certified PCMS instructor within the past three years.

RMC Subject Matter Expert personnel are also required to retain proficiency through annual accomplishment of at least one AP-1 and one RIP. This certification enables RMCs and shipyards to maintain a cadre of qualified PCMS personnel and with the assistance of the PCMS ISEA, to coordinate further certification or recertification training as required. Specific certification levels are addressed in the relevant PCMS Program NAVSEA manual. Training Requirements. Per reference (c) and (e), NAVSEA 05P1 has established the requirement that all personnel involved in PCMS installation and maintenance, including inspection/assessment, surface preparation, material application, final painting or quality assurance, must be U.S. citizens trained in the specifics of PCMS installation procedures prior to any actual tile installation work. As waterfront experience has underscored the absolute importance of limiting PCMS work to properly trained personnel, the certification process is the single most important element of quality assurance for the fleet customer. All personnel assigned PCMS repair duties must be trained in the requirements of reference (f). Regional Maintenance Center Japan, Regional Maintenance Center Rota and Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard. With the exception of CVN training, Forward Deployed Naval Forces (Regional Maintenance Center Japan, Regional Maintenance Center Rota and Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard) are authorized to execute training of personnel organic to their production codes for all PCMS maintenance and installation work using the PCMS ISEA provided training guide. Ship’s Force Personnel. Per the requirements of reference (c) MRC S-1, fleet personnel conducting PCMS S-1 assessments must be graduates of a PCMS ISEA approved ship supervisor course which includes an assessment/inspection training module. Ship’s Force personnel assigned maintainer duties to include all reference (d) MRCs except the S-1 must be graduates of the PCMS ISEA approved PCMS maintainer course. Ship’s Force personnel assigned maintenance duties to include all reference (g) MRCs must be graduates of the PCMS ISEA approved CVN specific course. PASSIVE COUNTERMEASURE SYSTEM TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. PCMS technical assistance is available through the local RMC. Distance support is also available, if required. RESPONSIBILITIES. a.

Commander, Naval Sea Systems Command: (1) Certify personnel, facilities, and activities in PCMS handling, Quality Assurance, application, and destruction. Maintain records for each RMC certification. (2) Provide Equipment Guide List (EGL) packages for AP-1, AP-2 and S-1 assessments. AP-2/S-1 is not applicable to CVN. (3) Incorporate and distribute ship configuration revisions submitted following AP-1 and AP-2 assessments. AP-2 is not applicable to CVN. (4) Conduct analysis of all measurements and provide Forces Afloat reports of results and recommendations. (5) Adjudicate all PCMS related requests for Departures from Specifications. (6) Designate a PCMS ISEA to function as the first line technical resource for Forces Afloat. (7) Coordinate PCMS in service activities with the broader Surface Maintenance Engineering Planning Program (SURFMEPP) organization and other activities, such as corrosion control programs. b. Navy Regional Maintenance Center: (1) Ensure that RMCs have adequate PCMS SMEs/technicians to support PCMS core activities defined in paragraph 37.1 of this chapter. Provide stewardship of RMC SMEs to ensure a seamless transition when personnel are scheduled for transfer or retirement. If qualified PCMS Technicians are not available at local RMC, the RMC should contact the following (in order of contact) for assistance: (a) Other RMCs. (b) PCMS ISEA (NSWC PHD). This request must include funding for the performance of the activity. (2) Ensure integration of PCMS SME support to all former SUPSHIP planning and execution of shipboard repairs and other upkeep performed under the auspices of the RMC organization. (3) Establish I-Level PCMS tiling support shops at RMCs with PCMS responsibilities. (4) Ensure the integration of PCMS restoration on all RMC conducted repairs and corrosion control projects where PCMS coverage is required.

This is to ensure that PCMS restoration requirements generated as interferences to work performed by I and D level activities are not assigned to Ship’s Force, but rather are restored as part of the I or D task. Should the Type Commander determine that it is necessary to abbreviate the funded task, he or she must direct the ship to submit a Departure from Specifications (DFS) to NAVSEA delineating the specifics of the unfunded PCMS restoration work. c. Type Commanders must: (1) Coordinate with the System Commands in identifying, solving and correcting PCMS deficiencies. (2) Refer all PCMS related Departures from Specifications to NAVSEA for adjudication. (3) Prior to promulgation, review and authorize all documents prepared by technical agencies that contain procedures relative to PCMS and the fleet PCMS program. (4) Evaluate comments and recommendations regarding the fleet PCMS program. If necessary, issue changes to existing policy and procedures. (5) Fund PCMS RIPs to provide for the additional RMC labor and material required to conduct these events at least bi-annually. (6) Ensure that proper corrosion control procedures are employed in the planning and execution of I and D Level maintenance affecting PCMS areas. References (f) and (h) provides detailed guidance. (7) Coordinate all aspects of scheduling ship measurements. (8) Provide for the restoration of all PCMS materials removed as interferences for other tasks. d. Immediate Superiors in the Chain of Command (ISIC) must: (1) Submit requests to schedule PCMS core activities for each unit to maintain unit currency in trained personnel and ship measurements. (2) Review and take the appropriate action to correct PCMS discrepancies for subordinate units. e. RMCs must: (1) Maintain qualified PCMS personnel and ensure assets are available to perform PCMS activities of paragraph 37.1 of this chapter, per reference (b). (2) Budget and provide travel funding to the ISEA for RMC personnel PCMS competency certifications, as required. As an alternative, the RMC person requiring certification can travel to Norfolk or San Diego for certification from the ISEA.

(3) Budget for RMC PCMS SME attendance of Annual Waterfront PCMS Standardization Program Reviews required reference (b). (4) Provide Technical Assistance via distance support or on site visit as appropriate. (5) Conduct PCMS core activities. Provide the following to NAVSEA PCMS ISEA within four weeks following AP-1 events: (a) Redlined updates to key plans and detailed drawings. (b) Completed EGL inspection checklist, including revised items. (c) Completed digital photo surveys consisting of any new systems and topside changes not previously submitted or not listed in the ship key plans. (6) Ensure that RMC PCMS SMEs are involved in planning of all PCMS equipped ship topside maintenance where PCMS is affected. (7) Ensure that RMC Quality Assurance personnel, certified by the PCMS ISEA, are actively involved in the Quality Assurance of all I and D level PCMS related repairs and installations. (8) Ensure that contracted or I-Level jobs activities, facilities and personnel selected to conduct PCMS work are certified for the work being conducted. (9) Conduct annual inventory of all locally RMC held PCMS materials and provide results to NAVSEA 05P1. (10) Include in contracted I and D-Level jobs the provision of PCMS tiles for planned PCMS repairs and interference areas. Ships must not be tasked to provide tiles or other PCMS Allowance Parts List or Allowance Equipage List items to support work undertaken by other than Ship's Force, except with the specific concurrence of the TYCOM. (11) Maintain repair capability detailed in paragraph 37 .1.1.g of this chapter. f. PCMS Ship Commanding Officers must ensure: (1) Scheduling of PCMS activities within periodicity. (2) Obtaining RMC SME assistance in reviewing work packages to ensure identification of all topside signature related issues. (3) Establishment and maintaining of the following shipboard organization: NOTE: AS OUTLINED IN CHAPTER 19, APPENDIX C4H OF THIS VOLUME, THE OT02 WORKCENTER IS DESIGNATED AS THE PCMS MAINTENANCE WORKCENTER.

CVN DOES NOT LIST A SPECIFIC PCMS WORKCENTER. REFERENCE (B) CONTAINS ALL CVN PCMS MAINTENANCE REQUIREMENTS AND MUST BE CARRIED UNDER WORKCENTER OS02 (ELECTRONIC WARFARE (EW) OR CRYPTOLOGIC TECHNICIAN, TECHNICAL (CTT)). ADDITIONALLY, THE CVN PCMS SUPERVISOR MUST COME FROM THIS WORKCENTER OR CAN BE A MORE SENIOR PERSON WITHIN THE SAME DEPARTMENT. (a) PCMS Department Head: Per reference (a), the Commanding Officer must appoint a Department Head responsible for coordinating operation and maintenance of PCMS. Their responsibilities include: 1 Providing the Commanding Officer monthly PCMS effectiveness summaries including major PCMS deficiencies, the compliance of the ship with personnel certification requirements, an abbreviated Plan of Action and Milestones for correction of Category 1, 2 and 3 deficiencies and corrosion items, and the due date for the next ship measurement. 2 Coordinating shipboard PCMS indoctrination for newly reported personnel. 3 Coordinating ship-wide PCMS preventive and corrective maintenance schedule. 4 Coordinating distribution and update of Planned Maintenance System (PMS) materials, including ship specific PCMS key plan drawings and EGLs required for PMS inspections. 5 Serving as single point of contact for Quality Assurance of PCMS related Current Ship's Maintenance Project entries, review of all topside configuration changes (including program alterations, fleet alterations, field changes, etc.) to ensure Radar Cross Section reduction has been considered. 6 Ensuring PCMS is included in the command PMS spot-check program. 7 Assigning a command PCMS coordinator responsible to the PCMS Department Head for the detailed implementation of PCMS maintenance and operation. 8 Designate in writing the maintenance assignments by all work centers assigned PCMS responsibility, as applicable. (b) Command PCMS coordinator: The command PCMS coordinator is the primary assistant to the PCMS Department Head in carrying out his or her responsibilities. Additional responsibilities include:

1 Request PCMS RIPs at intervals not to exceed 24 months (non-CVN). a Designate team of minimum 8 people (DDG and LPD), (15 people (CG) to attend the RIP. This team must include at least two supervisor level personnel (E5 and above). These team members must be committed throughout the entire RIP duration and cannot be substituted once the RIP commences. b Commit this team to the full 5-day period, arranging other individual requirements or commitments around the PCMS RIP. The names, rates and PRD of these personnel must be provided to the local RMC SME by e-mail or record message not later than 3 working days prior to the PCMS RIP. The senior ship’s force member of this team is responsible as the team’s mustering petty officer and must exercise military control of the team. Personnel may not be substituted once the RIP has begun. c All PCMS training requested through the RMC will be done by ship submission of a 2K. 2 Maintain personnel certifications, ensuring the required number of trained personnel are onboard. For DDG and LPD, a minimum of 8 maintainers and 2 supervisor-trained personnel are required. For CG, a minimum of 15 maintainers and 2 supervisor-trained personnel are required. For CVN, a minimum of 15 personnel are required to be trained in the CVN-specific training, one of which formerly designated as the ship’s PCMS Supervisor. 3 During RMC technical assists, ships would be expected to provide a minimum, dedicated team of five Level 1 Maintainer personnel and one Level I Supervisor personnel for such a technical assist. The team would be required to muster at least 80% of its assigned personnel continuously for workdays during the technical assistance period. (c) Supply Officer: Maintain Allowance Parts List stocks of PCMS materials and sufficient Allowance Equipage List items to support maintenance requirements. All shipboard stocks must be within shelf life.

VOLUME VI CHAPTER 38 DEEP SUBMERGENCE SYSTEMS HULL INTEGRITY PROCEDURES REFERENCES. (a) NAVSEA SS800-AG-MAN-010/P-9290 - System Certification Procedures and Criteria Manual for Deep Submergence Systems LISTING OF APPENDICES. A SUBMEPP DSS HIP Inventory B SUBMEPP DSS HIP Schedule C Request for DSS HIP Periodicity Extension Format PURPOSE. This chapter provides guidance and definition for the requirements, responsibilities and actions for Deep Submergence Systems (DSS) Hull Integrity Procedures (HIP) to continue certification for manned operations. The DSS HIP program is invoked on Dry Deck Shelter (DDS) certified under reference (a). HULL INTEGRITY PROCEDURES MAINTENANCE SCHEDULING, PLANNING AND REPORTING. Maintenance Requirements for Continued Certification. Reference (a) establishes the Maintenance Requirements and identifies the responsibilities and actions required to support continued unrestricted Submarine and DSS manned operations. In conjunction with reference (a), Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) has issued individual manuals containing required, periodic Scope of Certification (SOC) maintenance actions for each DSS. The DSS HIP procedures identify degradation of the material condition of the hull integrity boundary and of those systems affecting occupant safety. SOC certification indicates that a valid recommendation for continued manned operations can be made. Maintenance of certification is dependent on the positive control of all re-entries into the SOC boundaries per Volume V, Part III, Chapter 5 of this manual, the satisfactory and timely completion of applicable DSS HIP procedures as required by reference (a) and any necessary repairs. Accomplishment of the DSS HIPs specified with this program identify changes within the SOC boundary which result from inadvertent error or from degradation caused by the service environment. Scheduling and Reporting.
